page.layout: One block of text, a letter ending, running to the right edge of the scan where the lines are cut off. Below it: the place and date line, the addressee's title on two lines, and the closing lines with the signature, all at the right. No running head, page number or margin notes.

main_text.p: partam Te pluris facere, quà Religionis decus assertum. Ide Deum omnes supplices ven[illegible, ~6 letters] Te Reipublicæ [illegible, ~8 letters] bono servet, [illegible, ~3 letters] [?]tueatur incolumem, utqu[illegible, ~3 letters] diu rem feliciter & ex senten[illegible, ~3 letters] ria geras.
Trajecti ad Rhenum XIII. K[illegible, ~2 letters] Iun. MDCI[?] XXIX[?]

page.notes: The right edge of the scan cuts off the ends of most lines, so their last words are lost; I have marked only the gaps that are inside the lines. A large ink blot covers the start of the fourth and fifth lines and the middle of the fifth, so those readings are doubtful. The date line is partly broken: the Roman numerals in "cIↄ Iↄ" and "XXIX" are read with [?]. The word "Generof mo" is printed with a split across two lines and an s that looks like f; I have written the long s as plain s with [?]. Printed "clɔ" in the date is a reversed-C number; I rendered it as MDC with [?] because the scan is faint there.
